Kaduna State Government has clarified that the plan to hand over the Kaduna State Library Board Complex to the State High Court was never approved when the idea was mooted.
A statement issued by the Acting Director of Kaduna State Library Board, Amina Yahaya on Wednesday, stated that the Secretary to Kaduna State Government, Dr AbdulKadir Muázu Meyere has already put the matter to rest via a circular.
The Acting Director noted that policies usually undergo various stages of meetings and reviews, between when they are conceived and final decisions are taken by Government.
According to her, some newspapers published the purported handover of the Kaduna State Library Complex, before Governor Uba Sani granted the approval.
She said that the Secretary to the State Government’s circular noted that the Governor holds the Judiciary in the highest esteem and appreciates its indispensable role in the administration of justice, upholding the rule of law and safeguarding the rights of citizens in the State.
The statement said that the Kaduna State Government has been supporting the judiciary as demonstrated by the renovation of its facilities and the administration’s commitment to construct additional office accommodation across the State.
The Acting Director however argued that the governor’s support will not be at the expense of other legacy institutions of Government, especially the Kaduna State Library Board Headquarters.

According to her, the building serves as an important medium for the preservation and dissemination of information and knowledge, research and documentation for present and future generations.
The statement disclosed that the Ministry of Justice has been mandated to liaise with the Judiciary, to identify a suitable land for the construction of additional courtrooms and office accommodations.
